title: Quantum Topological Data Encoding
authors: Adam Wesołowski, Dimitrios Thanos, Daniel Leykam, Lirandë Pira
abstract: Many datasets encountered across a wide range of domains possess rich geometric and topological structure that is difficult to capture using conventional vector-based representations. Quantum machine learning offers the possibility of processing high-dimensional data in Hilbert spaces, but its practical success depends critically on how classical data is encoded into quantum states. We introduce \emph{quantum topological data encoding} (QTDE), a general framework for encoding topological information into quantum states via topology-driven quantum evolution. Our method generalises an existing topology-driven quantum encoding framework to higher-dimensional data. We test the proposed method on clique-complexes classification tasks, and provide preliminary evidence that topology-driven quantum representations can capture discriminative information beyond that available through direct comparisons of classical topological descriptors. The proposed quantum representations consistently outperform a baseline based on direct comparisons of the combinatorial Laplacians describing the underlying topological structure. We indicate several areas of application where the framework can be used to provide a more efficient and reliable data representation.
summary: The paper introduces Quantum Topological Data Encoding (QTDE), a general framework that encodes the topological structure of datasets into quantum states. It uses the combinatorial Laplacian as the generator for unitary quantum evolution, creating representations superior to classical methods. This advances quantum machine learning by providing a robust way to process high-dimensional data carrying complex geometric information.
main_problem: The core problem is developing a method to encode rich geometric and topological structure from classical datasets into quantum states for machine learning applications.
main_result: Quantum Topological Data Encoding (QTDE) successfully maps simplicial complexes to quantum states, showing that these representations outperform baselines derived from direct comparison of classical Laplacian descriptors.
method: The framework uses topology-driven quantum evolution, governed by the combinatorial Laplacian matrix ($L_k$), to generate quantum states $|\Psi(T)angle$. This is generalized using Quantum Singular Value Transformation (QSVT) for tunable spectral filtering.
model_or_system: The model involves mapping a dataset's structure (represented as a simplicial complex $K$) into a quantum state in a Hilbert space. The dynamics are dictated by the unitary evolution operator $U_k(t) = e^{-i L_k t}$, where $L_k$ is the combinatorial Laplacian.
key_observables: The primary observables include the resulting quantum state $|\Psi(T)angle$, the fidelity kernel $K = |\langle \Psi(T_1)|\Psi(T_2)angle|^2$, and explicit feature vectors derived from expectation values.
important_parameters: Key parameters involve the Laplacian dimension ($k$), time evolution parameter ($t$), and polynomial coefficients ($	heta$) used in QSVT.
main_assumptions: The method assumes that guiding quantum encoding via the topology itself is beneficial, rather than just extracting invariants; explicit representations rely on selecting a finite set of observables $\{M_j\}$ and times $\{t_j\}$.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the QTDE workflow (Classical data -> Laplacian -> Evolution -> Quantum Representation) and compare performance metrics like fidelity kernels ($K_{ij}$) and cosine similarity matrices derived from different spectral filters.
paper_structure: The paper introduces QTDE, details the use of the combinatorial Laplacian as a Hamiltonian generator for unitary evolution, proposes both implicit (kernel-based) and explicit (feature vector) representations, validates these methods on classification tasks, and discusses future directions like hardware implementation and complexity guarantees.
why_interesting: This work bridges algebraic topology with quantum computation by providing a concrete mechanism to embed complex relational data structures into the quantum domain using spectral properties of graph Laplacians.

figures.caption: FIG. 1: Overview of the Quantum Topological Data Encoding (QTDE) framework. Classical relational data are lifted to a simplicial complex, encoded by the combinatorial Laplacian Lk, and mapped to quantum representations through topology-driven evolution or spectral filtering implemented via quantum singular value transformation (QSVT). The resulting quantum representation can be accessed either implicitly through a fidelity-based quantum kernel or explicitly through features derived through measurement. Both representations provide topological feature maps that can be used in downstream machine learning tasks such as classification and prediction.

FIG. 2: Classification accuracy based on QTDE (using a support vector machine) as a function of simplicial dimension k for binary classification tasks on clique complexes based on Erdős–Rényi random graph ensembles. The three panels correspond to increasingly challenging discrimination tasks between topological-space classes generated based on random graphs with different edge probabilities. Results are shown for the proposed fidelity kernel representation (blue) and survival features (green), together with a classical baseline based on direct comparison of combinatorial Laplacians through a matrix-difference kernel (brown).
